x: Article 371D gives special provisions for Andhra Pradesh. The other pairs are wrong: Article 371 covers Maharashtra and Gujarat (not Mizoram), Article 371A is Nagaland (not Goa), and Article 371J is Karnataka (Sikkim is under Article 371F).

Article 131 is the SC's original jurisdiction in Centre-State disputes (iv); Article 136 is Special Leave (iii); Article 143 is advisory jurisdiction on Presidential reference (ii); Article 227 is HC superintendence over subordinate courts (i). Option B swaps 131 and 136; option C swaps 136 and 143; option D gets only 136 right and mismatches 131, 143 and 227.

Article 215 makes every High Court a court of record, with power to punish contempt of itself. Article 226 concerns writs (not salaries), Article 227 superintendence (district judges are appointed under Article 233), and Article 218 applies the SC judges' removal procedure to HC judges, not contempt.

Confirmation of Sessions Court death sentences by the High Court is now governed by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the CrPC from 1 July 2024. The CPC is civil procedure, the IPC is substantive criminal law, and the Contempt of Courts Act deals with contempt.

Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Governor appoints District Judges in consultation with the High Court, and a direct recruit needs 7 years as an advocate or pleader. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 233 requires such a person not to be already in the service of the Union or the State, so seven years at the Bar alone does not make a government servant eligible.

The Armed Forces Tribunal was set up under the Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007. The other pairs are mismatched: NCLT is under the Companies Act, 2013; CESTAT under the Customs Act, 1962; and Debt Recovery Tribunals under the Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993 (the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 governs CGIT-cum-Labour Courts).
